sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement (virtual/physical) mode.

2. This is the successive journey of the Petitioner, who apprehends his arrest in connection with Nabarangpur P.S. Case No.483 of 2021 T.R Case No.59 of 2021, pending on the file of learned Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge, Nabarangpur running for the alleged commission of offence under section 366/376(2)(n)/506/34 of the IPC read with section 3(1)(r)/3(1)(s) and 3(2)(v) of SC &
ST (POA) Act, in filing this application under section 438, Cr.P.C., for his release on bail in the event of his arrest.

3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that although the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the Petitioner was earlier rejected, in view of emergence of changing circumstances, the Petitioner is moving for the second time..

He submits that the son of this Petitioner is the principal accused against against whom, the allegations with regard to the commission of principal offences run and he having faced the enquiry as Child in Conflict with Law (CCL) before the Juvenile Justice Board,
Nabarangpur has in the meantime been acquitted since the victim stated nothing as regards the commission of the offences by the CCL or against anyone.

He further submits that when the Juvenile Justice Board has released the CCL without recording any finding as to his guilt, the likely arrest and detention of the Petitioner who happens to be the father of the principal accused at this stage would not serve no useful purpose for the case.

4. Learned counsel for the State opposes the move.

He however does not dispute the position that in the mean time, the principal accused, who is the son of the Petitioner having faced the trial has been released since the victim herself did not implicate him in any manner in the matter of commission of crime nor stated against anyone else.

5. Considering the submissions made and on going through the materials available on record especially the deposition of the victim recorded in the enquiry before the Juvenile Justice Board,
Nabarangpur, finding the changes in the circumstances; while being inclined to reconsider the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the Petitioner, it is directed that in the event, the Petitioner surrenders before the Court in seissin of the aforesaid case within two weeks hence and moves for his release on bail, he shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as would be deemed just and proper by the said Court.
6. The ABLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
